nodes.summary: The unbounded knapsack problem is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of unbounded knapsack instances, to a feasible instance. Bitstrings that fail to decode are rejected.
nodes.title: Unbounded knapsack as a decision problem

nodes.summary: An unbounded knapsack instance with items $(s_1, v_1), \dots, (s_m, v_m)$, capacity $C$ and target value $K$ is feasible when there are multiplicities $c_1, \dots, c_m \in \mathbb{N}$ with $\sum_{j=1}^{m} c_j s_j \le C$ and $\sum_{j=1}^{m} c_j v_j \ge K$.
nodes.title: Feasible unbounded knapsack instances

nodes.summary: An instance of the unbounded knapsack problem is a triple $(I, C, K)$ of a finite list $I = ((s_1, v_1), \dots, (s_m, v_m))$ of items, where item $j$ has weight $s_j \in \mathbb{N}$ and value $v_j \in \mathbb{N}$, a capacity $C \in \mathbb{N}$ and a target value $K \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Unbounded knapsack instances

nodes.summary: The unbounded knapsack decision problem belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.
nodes.title: UNBOUNDED KNAPSACK is NP-complete

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
